Oval progress rose to 0.46 (from 0.12), but s-bend (0.16) and slalom (0.10) still end early. Every run still ends off-track, with rms_error near 0.03 and max_error at 0.061 to 0.067. Oval max_error exceeded the 0.06 target, so the prediction was only partly met. Mass and track changed together with the footprint, so their effects are not separated.\n\nThe key evidence is the line-loss timing. Each run logs exactly one line-loss event, and max_error sits at the 0.06 limit on every track. Geometry explains this. The outer sensors sit at x = ±0.04. A 16 mm footprint there reaches to about ±0.048. A 25 mm tape adds its half-width of 0.0125, so the sensor stops seeing any tape once the line centre passes about 0.06 m. That is the same distance as the off-track limit. When the array loses the line, the sum of readings drops below 0.05, the controller switches to the fixed line-loss signal, and the robot leaves the tape with no useful steering. The 0.06 excursion is therefore a sensing dead zone at the edge of the array's reach, not only a turn-rate limit.\n\nDecision: widen the outer sensors to x = ±0.06 and set the inner three at ±0.03 and 0, so spacing is uniform at 0.03 m. Keep 16 mm footprints. At 0.03 m pitch, the gap between neighbouring footprints is 0.014 m, and a line centred between two sensors still gives overlap on both (about 0.34 each), so there is no dead zone inside the array. With the outer centres at ±0.06, the outer sensor still reads tape out to about 0.08 m from centre (0.06 + 0.008 + 0.0125 ≈ 0.08), so the line stays visible past the off-track limit. I am keeping the body (0.5 kg, 0.10 m track) and the forward row at y = 0.04 unchanged, so the result isolates the reach change. Turn authority is the next variable if max_error stays at 0.06.\n\nExpected result: line_loss_events fall to zero or stay at one only at the final exit; max_error drops below 0.06 on the s-bend and slalom; and progress rises on all three tracks.
